bench: Agentic baseline (E1): an external LLM agent drives the validated tools, audited for no-fabrication
question: When a real LLM agent (not the deterministic state machine) drives PEN-STACK's validated tools, does every number in its trace equal a direct tool call (no fabrication)? Does this hold across the model-capability range?
method: For each write-planning goal, the LLM (via pen_stack.agent.orchestrator.run_agent) plans and calls the validated design tools itself; pen_stack.validate.agent_eval.no_fabrication audits that every quantity in the returned plan is traceable to a tool result. Two distinct quantities are recorded and must not be read as one: llm_driven_runs counts goals where the LLM orchestrator was in control rather than the deterministic fallback, and goals_with_tool_calls counts goals where it actually issued a tool call. A goal answered in prose issues no call, emits no quantity, and so passes the audit with nothing audited.
goals: insert a durable cassette at AAVS1
write into CCR5 for HIV resistance
place a durable transgene at CLYBL

deterministic_gate.note: the grounded state machine (no LLM); runs everywhere incl. CI

finding: Across three models spanning a 1.5B local model to hosted cloud models, the no-fabrication audit passed in every run: every quantity that was emitted equalled a direct tool call. Tool engagement was uneven, at 11 of 12 model-goal runs issuing at least one call; the remaining 1 answered in prose and so passed with no quantity to audit. The audit therefore establishes that no ungrounded quantity was emitted, not that the tools were driven throughout. A matched run over the full goal set is reported separately.

provenance.reproduce: python bench/run.py --agent  (with a reachable provider set in configs/llm.yaml)
provenance.note: nemotron+claude run against their cloud APIs (keys gitignored); qwen2.5:1.5b runs locally via Ollama.
